brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Storey 1 is the ground cluster of bases (0,0),(1,0),(1,-1) plus drawers; storey 2 is a full base at (0,0,1) stacked on the tower. The second storey is a single cell, not a full layer; no drawers or bins are on it.
The tower is a compact hex cluster sized for a bench, but no bench mounting or footprint check was made beyond the configurator's fit and collision checks.
Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) at notch:0#0,-1 and notch:0#0,1 on the ground storey, each between two touching bases.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex storage tower: a ground-level cluster of three full bases at (0,0), (1,0), (1,-1), with a full base stacked on (0,0) at level 1 as the second storey. Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) fill the empty ground-level positions at (0,-1) and (0,1), each between two touching bases. Open faces are closed with solid caps and joints are bolted (lockJoints). check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear. The build was not dressed with props, since the brief is about storage only.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
